text: Around the world, countries are making a gradual transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources such as solar power, wind, and hydropower. Unlike coal and oil, which are finite resources that will eventually run out, renewable energy comes from sources that nature constantly replaces, like sunlight and wind. Modern wind turbines can generate a huge amount of clean electricity without producing the harmful emissions associated with fossil fuels. However, building this new infrastructure requires a large investment, and many governments offer a subsidy to encourage companies to install solar panels and turbines. One challenge is that renewable energy is not always reliable, since solar power depends on sunshine and wind turbines need enough wind to generate electricity. To solve this, engineers are developing innovative ways to store energy and connect it to the power grid, so supply can meet demand even when conditions change. As technology improves, the capacity and output of renewable energy systems continue to grow, making them a more realistic alternative to fossil fuels. Experts believe that if this transition continues at its current pace, renewable resources could provide most of the world's electricity within a few decades, significantly reducing our reliance on fossil fuels.
